inserts.afterExact: Most Hindu temples feature intricate painted sculptures and carved gopurams. The Sri Rajakaliamman temple took a different approach: beginning in the 1990s, the community began covering every interior surface with hand-set glass tiles in jewel-toned colours — blue, green, gold, red, and white. The process took years and continues to be refined. The result is that even at midday, when natural light enters through coloured glass panels, the interior glows.

The temple is dedicated to Goddess Kaliamman, a form of the goddess Kali worshipped primarily by Tamil Hindus. It serves as an active place of worship for JB's Indian community, not just a tourist attraction — visitors are asked to behave respectfully, remove shoes, and speak quietly inside.

officialSection:
Official Information

  • Address: Jalan Tun Abdul Razak 1/1, Wadihana, 80300 Johor Bahru. Tourism Johor
  • Opening hours: 10.00 am – 10.00 pm, open every day. Tourism Johor
  • Entrance fee: RM10.00. Tourism Johor
  • History: established in 1922; about 95% of the walls, ceiling and pillars are covered with stained-glass mirrors imported from Thailand, Japan and Belgium. Tourism Johor

Details above were checked against the Tourism Johor listing on 1 October 2026. Temple hours and fees can change, so confirm with the temple before you go.
